what: The database proxy: the one door a box's processes reach their database by (outline 11.3). v0 is a byte relay, its own process, listening on 127.0.0.1:5432 and forwarding to the box's own Postgres on its local port (CAIRN_DBPROXY_POSTGRES_PORT, default 5433).
why: Every table has one owner who gates every write, and the authentication is wrapped up in the proxy (outline 11.3.1), so a box needs one address its database is reached at. Each box runs its own instance and everything on the box talks only to it (11.3.7). On a cache box Postgres sits on another port so that 5432 is the proxy's.
owner: CC owns dbproxy's code and proofs and gates writes to them; the spec is outline 11.3 (Akien's).
falsifier: RED when bytes written to the relay do not reach the upstream and the upstream's reply does not come back, for two concurrent connections kept apart; when the listener is bound anywhere but 127.0.0.1 only; when, with the listen port already held (the home box), the process does not exit 0 with its record saying held and forwarding nothing; when an upstream that refuses leaves the client's connection open or the refusal uncounted; when waking the device does not spawn its own process (a pid not the waker's) that listens on the listen port and writes its record, or a second wake spawns more, or on Windows the spawn does not take background_pythonw and detached_kwargs; when the shim's device_id or the charter's answers_as is not database. Proof: proofs/test_the_database_proxy_forwards_to_postgres.py.
gates: proof gate: proofs/test_the_database_proxy_forwards_to_postgres.py, run by the tester. Durability gate: proven and committed.
invoke: cairn database start (the bus wakes the device face, which spawns `python -m cairn.devices.dbproxy` windowless when it is not running); cairn database show status.
public_interface: the bus: `cairn database` (start, show status, show settings)
how_it_learns: It does not yet: v0 relays bytes and counts connections and refusals in its record. Learning arrives with the owner gate and the sync, which read what passes through.
state_and_history: its runtime record (pid, ports, state, counts) lives in instance space under devices/dbproxy/0; no state in class-space.
